I've been farming this 40 mu piece of land for 6 years now. I'm 51, never went to school, but I watch and I learn. My neighbor Old Wang has farmed for 30 years and I pay attention to what he does. He says if it works, don't change it, and that's how I farm too. There's three of us at home but it's mostly my wife and me doing the field work.

This year I'll plant wheat on all 40 mu in mid-October, same as always. I saved some seed from last year but not enough, so I'll buy more from the shop in town. The local wheat seed does fine here, no need for expensive fancy kinds.

For fertilizer, before planting I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the regular kind from the shop, the one with the three numbers on the bag. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I topdress with about half a bag of urea per mu. That's what I've done these 6 years and it works. I don't count jin or kilos — I just know one bag and half a bag. Old Wang uses about the same. Fertilizer got more expensive this year but I'd rather use a bit too much than too little. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps, and I can't afford to lose the crop. Better to waste some fertilizer than risk an empty grain head.

I'll water the wheat three times — once at planting if the ground is dry, once when the stems start growing fast, and once when the grain is filling. Pumping from the well costs money so I don't water for nothing, but three times is right if it rains a little too.

After wheat harvest in early June, I have to get the maize in quick — sometimes less than a week. I hire a combine to cut the wheat, then either till quick with the rotary tiller or just plant straight if I'm running late. I buy that hybrid maize seed from the shop — the yellow bags, everyone plants it. Costs more but grows strong. I put one bag of compound fertilizer in the row when I plant the maize. Maize is easier than wheat — maybe one more watering when it's getting tall, and spray for weeds.

My wife helps with everything and we do most of the work ourselves, but at wheat harvest and maize planting we hire a few people for several days. Forty mu is too much for two people when the timing is everything. We also hire the combine and sometimes a tractor with driver.

I spray herbicide on both crops — weeds will take over if you don't. If I see bugs eating the leaves I'll spray for them, but I don't waste money spraying for nothing.

Last year I got about 450 jin per mu of wheat and 500 jin of maize. If the weather is normal I expect about the same. I know my field pretty well after 6 years — which spots are good and which stay wet.

All together I'll spend about 18,000 or 19,000 yuan on seeds, fertilizer, chemicals, water, and hired help. That's a lot for us. I have some money put aside but I always keep cash in hand — you never know when the pump breaks or someone needs the doctor. Better to have money ready than to spend it all on the crop.
